answer: An identity claims an island lease after a voyage, then lists it on the velvet roll at a self-assessed price and pays 5% tax each epoch. Anyone may buy from the velvet roll at the assessed price, so a low-priced fake is bought out, while a fake priced at 1,000 pays 50 tax. Each fake needs its own voyage and lease, so the kth fake still pays full tax and 1,000 fakes at 1,000 pay 50,000 tax per epoch, without pooling. A squatting ring fails: its cheapest leases are bought first, forcing prices up. An honest agent holds one island lease at true price and pays one tax.
